sections.name: Analytical Data Preparation and Exploration
sections.outcome: Transform heterogeneous records into analysis-ready tables and characterize their quality, distributions, group differences, and relationships.

sample_tasks.instruction: Standardize the types and labels in a small table, then report one distributional feature of the corrected data.

Using one collection of customer, transaction, and account records, construct an analysis-ready table, diagnose consequential quality problems, summarize its variables and groups, and investigate relationships relevant to customer retention.

sections.name: Analytical Data Preparation
sections.outcome: Clean, transform, combine, and reshape tabular records into analysis-ready observations and variables while preserving their meaning and grain.
excludes: Schema compliance as the primary outcome

sample_tasks.instruction: Convert a small table's date and amount columns to consistent types and derive one requested indicator.

Prepare one set of order and customer tables by normalizing types and categories, filtering invalid records, deriving requested measures, joining at the correct grain, reshaping repeated monthly fields, and documenting justified missing-value treatment.

sections.name: Tabular Cleaning and Feature Construction
sections.outcome: Normalize analytical variables and apply justified row selection, recoding, missing-value treatment, and feature derivation without changing observational meaning.
includes: Type, unit, category, and date normalization
excludes: Detecting quality problems without repairing data

sample_tasks.instruction: Normalize one mixed-format date column and recode one inconsistent category column in a small table.

Clean a transaction table by resolving duplicate observations, normalizing dates, units, and categories, applying stated inclusion rules, treating missing values according to their meanings, and deriving analysis variables at the original row grain.

sections.name: Table Integration and Reshaping
sections.outcome: Join, aggregate, and reshape normalized tables at an explicit observational grain while preventing duplication, loss, and leakage.

sample_tasks.instruction: Normalize the keys, types, categories, missing values, and requested derived field in two small tables, then add one many-to-one lookup column without changing the row count.

Normalize and recode customer, order, and monthly-status tables, derive the requested fields, then join, aggregate, and reshape them to one customer-month row per observation while reconciling unmatched keys, duplicated totals, and leakage-prone fields.

sections.name: Exploratory Data Analysis
sections.outcome: Diagnose data quality and use descriptive and relationship analysis to reveal distributions, anomalies, group differences, and plausible analytical directions.

sample_tasks.instruction: Inspect a small numeric column, identify one invalid value, and describe the valid values with an appropriate center and spread.

Explore one service-use table by diagnosing quality problems, selecting summaries for its numeric and categorical variables, comparing customer groups, and investigating whether apparent outcome relationships persist across relevant strata and after checking artifacts.

sections.name: Data Quality Diagnosis
sections.outcome: Detect and characterize missingness, invalid values, duplicates, inconsistent units, and measurement artifacts that could distort an analysis.
excludes: Format validation as the primary task

sample_tasks.instruction: Identify the values in a short measurement column that violate its stated range or unit.

Audit a multi-table operational dataset for invalid values, duplicate entities, inconsistent units, temporal coverage gaps, and systematic missingness, and explain how each problem could alter the intended analysis.

sections.name: Distribution and Group Summaries
sections.outcome: Select and compute summaries that accurately describe central tendency, spread, shape, frequency, and differences among defined groups.
excludes: Association after conditioning on other variables

sample_tasks.instruction: Compute the median and interquartile range of a skewed numeric sample and explain why they are suitable.

Summarize mixed numeric and categorical variables across customer segments, choosing measures that expose skew, dispersion, rare categories, and within-group variation while retaining relevant group sizes.

sections.name: Exploratory Relationship Analysis
sections.outcome: Characterize associations while distinguishing form, direction, strength, subgroup heterogeneity, conditioning effects, and possible artifacts.
excludes: Group summaries with no relationship question

sample_tasks.instruction: For a small mixed-type table, compute suitable centers, spreads, frequencies, and group summaries, then add one stratified cross-tabulation to determine whether an apparent group difference reverses after conditioning on a third variable.

Summarize the distributions and group differences in an outcome and its candidate predictors, then characterize their linear and nonlinear associations, stratify by a relevant group, examine interaction and imbalance, and determine whether outliers or conditioning explain the initial pattern.

sections.name: Probability and Statistical Inference
sections.outcome: Represent uncertainty with probability models and use sample evidence to estimate, test, or bound population quantities with justified conclusions.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define a success event for a repeated process, calculate its one-trial probability, and distinguish that probability from an observed sample proportion.

For one service process, construct a probability model for completion and waiting time, update a probability after observing a diagnostic signal, use a sample to estimate and test the population completion rate, and obtain a separate tail bound when only moments are trusted.

sections.name: Probability Modeling
sections.outcome: Represent random events, information updates, and long-run quantities with explicit probability models.
excludes: Descriptive summaries without a random model

sample_tasks.instruction: List the outcomes of a two-stage random process and calculate the probability of one compound event.

Model one sequential inspection process by deriving its finite and eventual completion probabilities, updating the defect probability after an imperfect signal, and calculating the expected number and variance of inspections until acceptance.

sections.name: Events and Repeated Trials
sections.outcome: Construct sample spaces and calculate probabilities of simple, compound, complementary, and repeated events, including finite and eventual occurrence.

sample_tasks.instruction: Count the outcomes satisfying a condition in one roll of two fair dice and convert the count to a probability.

For independent trials that stop at a target event or a fixed limit, derive the probabilities of early completion, failure by the limit, and eventual completion, including all boundary parameter values.

sections.name: Conditional Probability and Updating
sections.outcome: Update probability assignments from observations or reports while making priors, conditioning events, information states, and evidence reliability explicit.
excludes: Claims unsupported by the probability model

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a disease prior, sensitivity, and false-positive rate for an imperfect test, calculate the probability of disease after a positive result.

Compare two analysts' probability assignments as one observes a noisy signal and communicates it through an imperfect channel, calculating each posterior and explaining how their distinct information states produce different answers.

sections.name: Expectation and Stopping Quantities
sections.outcome: Compute and interpret expectations, variances, and waiting times from specified random-variable and stopping models.
excludes: Observed averages without a probability model

sample_tasks.instruction: Construct the simple, compound, complementary, finite-repeat, and eventual event probabilities for a bounded sequence of independent trials, then add the expected number of trials used.

For a multistage process, construct its event space and finite and eventual completion probabilities, then define the stopping variables and derive the expected completion time and its variance when stages can repeat.

sections.name: Statistical Inference
sections.outcome: Use sampling behavior and stated assumptions to estimate population quantities, quantify uncertainty, test claims, and derive distribution-free moment bounds.
excludes: Pure probability calculations without sample evidence

sample_tasks.instruction: Explain how estimates from repeated random samples vary and use that variation to quantify uncertainty for one sample estimate.

For one quality-control sample, characterize an estimator's sampling behavior, report a point estimate and interval, test a directional claim, and derive a separate tail-count bound using only the supplied moments.

sections.name: Sampling Distributions and Standard Errors
sections.outcome: Relate a sampling design and repeated-sample variation to an estimator's bias, standard error, shape, and effective sample size.

sample_tasks.instruction: From estimates produced by several repeated random samples, calculate their empirical standard error.
Compare the repeated-sample distributions of an estimator under simple random, clustered, and stratified sampling, assessing bias, shape, standard error, and effective sample size.

sections.name: Estimation and Confidence Intervals
sections.outcome: Define estimands, compute point estimates and standard errors, and construct intervals whose interpretation matches the sampling design and assumptions.

sample_tasks.instruction: Characterize the bias, shape, standard error, and effective sample size of a mean under the stated sampling design, then add a confidence interval using that standard error.

For a stratified population survey, define the target rate, derive the weighted estimator's sampling behavior and standard error, construct a confidence interval, and explain its repeated-sampling coverage and design assumptions.

sections.name: Hypothesis Testing
sections.outcome: Formulate hypotheses, select and compute an appropriate test, check its assumptions, and state an error-aware decision in context.
excludes: Treating non-rejection as proof of equality

sample_tasks.instruction: Define the estimand, estimate it with a design-appropriate standard error and confidence interval, then add a one-sided null and alternative and compare the resulting p-value with one stated test size.

Estimate a manufacturing variance with uncertainty, formulate a directional claim, select and compute the appropriate reference-distribution test, check its assumptions, compare the p-value with several prespecified sizes, and report a contextual decision without treating non-rejection as proof.

sections.name: Moment-Based Probability Bounds
sections.outcome: Use means, second moments, and variances to derive justified one-sided or two-sided bounds on tail probabilities and counts without assuming a full distribution.
includes: Variance from first and second moments
excludes: Exact tails from a named distribution

sample_tasks.instruction: Use a supplied nonnegative mean to bound the proportion of values above a positive threshold.

Given a dataset size, mean, root-mean-square value, and cutoff, derive the variance, choose the strongest justified moment inequality, and convert its tail-probability bound into a valid integer count bound.

sections.name: Experiments and Population Health
sections.outcome: Design controlled comparisons and analyze biomedical or population-health evidence with measurements, statistical methods, biases, and decisions matched to the scientific question.

sample_tasks.instruction: For a proposed health intervention, identify one control and one outcome needed for a valid comparison.

For one population-health intervention, validate its biomarker measurement, design and analyze a randomized comparison, analyze repeated biomarker and event-time outcomes, estimate population disease associations, and state a decision that accounts for uncertainty and bias.

sections.name: Controlled Experiments and A/B Analysis
sections.outcome: Validate measurements, design randomized comparisons, and analyze experimental effects using prespecified outcomes, uncertainty, guardrails, and decision rules.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a negative control and a randomized comparison to a simple intervention study, naming the primary outcome.

For one randomized biomarker intervention, design matched measurement controls, choose assignment units and blocking, plan sample size and stopping, validate exposure and outcomes, estimate the treatment effect with a prespecified test, assess guardrails, and apply the decision rule.

sections.name: Controlled Measurement Validation
sections.outcome: Design matched controls and complementary measurements that distinguish a target signal or mechanism from contamination, artifact, and competing explanations.
excludes: Instrument calibration without a scientific contrast

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a negative control that tests whether fluorescence can arise without viable target cells.

Design a follow-up study that distinguishes true metabolic fluorescence from dead material, environmental debris, and instrument background using matched live and killed controls, localization, an independent viability measure, and explicit interpretation criteria.

sections.name: Randomized Experiment Design
sections.outcome: Specify assignment units, randomization, blocking, outcomes, sample size, exposure checks, stopping, and multiplicity controls for a valid randomized comparison.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose the assignment unit and randomization scheme for a two-variant test where users can influence one another.

Design a randomized product experiment by defining units and eligibility, handling interference with blocking or clustering, specifying primary and guardrail outcomes, planning sample size, checking exposure, and prespecifying stopping and multiplicity rules.

sections.name: A/B Experiment Analysis
sections.outcome: Integrate randomized-design and hypothesis-testing decisions to estimate variant effects, audit execution, assess guardrails, and make a prespecified launch decision.

sample_tasks.instruction: Design a two-arm experiment with explicit units, eligibility, randomization, blocking, outcomes, sample size, exposure checks, stopping, and multiplicity; formulate and carry out the primary hypothesis test with an estimate and interval; then add one guardrail threshold to the final decision.

Design and analyze a randomized product experiment by specifying assignment, blocking, outcomes, sample size, stopping and multiplicity; auditing assignment, exposure, and measurement; estimating primary and guardrail effects with assumption-aware tests and intervals; and applying the prespecified launch rule.

sections.name: Biostatistics and Epidemiology
sections.outcome: Analyze biomedical and population data using outcome-appropriate statistical methods, disease-frequency measures, study-design reasoning, and bias-aware interpretation.
excludes: Laboratory control design as the central task

sample_tasks.instruction: From a small cohort table, calculate disease risk by exposure group and identify whether one biomarker was measured repeatedly.

Analyze one cohort by modeling its repeated biomarker measurements and censored event times, estimating disease frequency and exposure association, and assessing confounding, selection, measurement bias, and clinical relevance.

sections.name: Biostatistical Outcome Analysis
sections.outcome: Analyze correlated longitudinal measurements and censored event times using methods whose assumptions and effect summaries match the biomedical outcome.
excludes: Population-level bias analysis as the central operation

sample_tasks.instruction: Identify whether a before-and-after biomarker comparison is paired and whether follow-up times include censoring.

For one patient cohort, analyze repeated biomarker measurements and time to relapse, accounting for within-patient dependence and censoring, checking method assumptions, and reporting uncertainty and clinical relevance for both outcomes.

sections.name: Paired and Longitudinal Outcome Analysis
sections.outcome: Analyze paired or repeated biomedical measurements while accounting for within-subject dependence, time, missing follow-up, and clinically meaningful change.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define and estimate a biomarker-change estimand with an interval, formulate and conduct an assumption-aware test with a contextual decision, then add the paired-subject structure rather than treating measurements as independent.

Analyze a longitudinal biomarker study by defining clinically meaningful contrasts, estimating repeated-measure effects with uncertainty, formulating and testing the relevant hypotheses, checking distributional and dependence assumptions, addressing missing follow-up, and interpreting time-by-treatment differences.

sections.name: Survival and Event-Time Analysis
sections.outcome: Estimate and compare time-to-event outcomes while handling censoring, risk sets, competing events, and proportionality or functional-form assumptions.

sample_tasks.instruction: Construct the first two risk sets for a small event-time dataset containing one censored observation.

Analyze time to relapse in two treatment groups by describing censoring, estimating survival or cumulative incidence, reporting an effect with uncertainty, checking proportionality and competing-event assumptions, and interpreting absolute and relative differences.

sections.name: Epidemiologic Measures and Bias
sections.outcome: Use study design, disease-frequency measures, association estimates, stratification, and bias analysis to interpret population-health evidence.
excludes: Statistical computation detached from study design

sample_tasks.instruction: Compute and interpret a risk ratio from exposed and unexposed event counts.

Evaluate an observational exposure study by selecting appropriate frequency and association measures, stratifying on a plausible confounder, assessing effect modification, and explaining the likely direction of selection and measurement biases.

sections.name: Model Assessment, Econometrics, and Forecasting
sections.outcome: Assess empirical models and claims, estimate economic relationships under explicit identification assumptions, and construct and evaluate forecasts for time-dependent data.
excludes: Domain knowledge as a substitute for supplied model assumptions
Presentation design as the primary outcome

sample_tasks.instruction: Compare one observed pattern with a supplied model prediction and state whether the discrepancy affects description, causal interpretation, or forecasting.

Using one policy panel and its time series, diagnose a supplied model's validity, estimate the policy relationship under competing identification designs, construct and backtest a forecast, and separate the decision-relevant evidence from claims the analysis does not support.

sections.name: Model and Evidence Assessment
sections.outcome: Use empirical discrepancies to diagnose where supplied assumptions fail and calibrate conclusions to what the analysis establishes.
excludes: Parameter estimation as the central task
Metaphysical interpretation detached from an analysis

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a stated model assumption and an observed residual pattern, identify one conclusion that follows and one stronger conclusion that does not.

For one supplied mechanistic model and dataset, compare predictions with observations across regimes, trace residual patterns to specific assumptions or boundaries, state the defensible validity domain, and distinguish the supported empirical conclusion from causal or mechanistic alternatives.

sections.name: Assumption and Validity-Regime Diagnostics
sections.outcome: Relate empirical residual and association patterns to explicit model assumptions, scale regimes, boundary conditions, and omitted dynamics supplied in the task.
excludes: Rejecting a model because of any mismatch

sample_tasks.instruction: Summarize distributions and group differences, characterize linear and nonlinear associations across strata, and check heterogeneity, imbalance, and outliers; then add one residual-pattern comparison to identify which supplied model assumption fails first.

Explore the outcome and predictors with distributional, grouped, nonlinear, stratified, interaction, imbalance, and artifact checks, then compare the resulting residual patterns with supplied scaling, boundary, and omitted-process assumptions to state the model's defensible validity regime.

sections.name: Empirical Evidence and Claim Calibration
sections.outcome: State what a completed analysis supports while distinguishing descriptive, predictive, causal, and mechanistic claims and identifying compatible alternatives.
excludes: Probability updating as the central calculation

sample_tasks.instruction: Rewrite a causal headline about an observational association as a claim supported by the reported analysis.

Assess an empirical analysis whose association fits several causal or mechanistic accounts, state the common supported finding with its uncertainty, compare compatible alternatives, and explain which additional design or evidence would distinguish them.

sections.name: Econometric Analysis
sections.outcome: Estimate economically meaningful relationships and evaluate causal interpretations using regression diagnostics and explicit quasi-experimental assumptions.

sample_tasks.instruction: Estimate and interpret the slope relating price to demand without calling it causal, then name one source of identifying variation that could support a causal estimate.

For one policy outcome, specify and diagnose an economic regression, then evaluate difference-in-differences, instrumental-variable, and discontinuity evidence tied to that same policy question before stating the most credible effect claim.

sections.name: Econometric Estimation and Diagnostics
sections.outcome: Specify, estimate, and interpret regression models while checking functional form, dependence, heteroskedasticity, leverage, and economically meaningful effect size.

sample_tasks.instruction: Summarize distributions and group differences, explore nonlinear and stratified associations and artifacts, define an estimand, characterize its sampling uncertainty, and construct an interval; then add a regression coefficient interpreted in the variables' economic units.

Explore an economic outcome and its predictors for distributions, group differences, nonlinearities, heterogeneity, imbalance, and artifacts; specify a multivariable regression; estimate interpretable effects and design-aware intervals; and diagnose functional form, dependence, heteroskedasticity, and influence without making an unsupported causal claim.

sections.name: Quasi-Experimental Identification
sections.outcome: Choose and assess difference-in-differences, instrumental-variable, and regression-discontinuity strategies for one causal question using each design's distinct source of variation and falsification checks.

sample_tasks.instruction: For one policy question, distinguish the identifying variation offered by a treatment-timing change, an instrument, and an eligibility cutoff.

For one policy-effect question with panel, instrument, and cutoff data available, formulate difference-in-differences, instrumental-variable, and regression-discontinuity analyses, test each design's central assumptions, and select the most credible estimate while explaining remaining threats.

sections.name: Difference-in-Differences Designs
sections.outcome: Estimate effects from differential treatment timing while assessing parallel trends, composition, anticipation, dynamics, and treatment heterogeneity.

sample_tasks.instruction: Specify and estimate a panel regression with economically interpreted effects, robust uncertainty, and residual, dependence, heteroskedasticity, and influence checks; then add one pre-treatment trend comparison before interpreting the post-treatment coefficient causally.

Specify and diagnose an economically interpretable panel model with robust uncertainty, then estimate a policy effect using difference-in-differences, examine pre-trends, anticipation, composition, dynamics, and heterogeneous timing, and report the causal claim warranted by those checks.

sections.name: Instrumental-Variable Designs
sections.outcome: Estimate local causal effects from an instrument while assessing relevance, exclusion, independence, monotonicity, weak-instrument risk, and estimand scope.
excludes: Treating any predictor as an instrument

sample_tasks.instruction: Specify and estimate the outcome regression with economic interpretation, robust uncertainty, and functional-form, dependence, heteroskedasticity, and influence diagnostics; then add a first-stage relevance check for one proposed instrument.

Specify and diagnose the economic outcome and first-stage regressions, estimate the effect by instrumental variables with robust uncertainty, assess relevance, exclusion, independence, monotonicity, and weak-instrument risk, and interpret the resulting local estimand.

sections.name: Regression-Discontinuity Designs
sections.outcome: Estimate local cutoff effects while assessing assignment continuity, manipulation, bandwidth, functional form, covariate balance, and placebo cutoffs.
excludes: Instrumental variation away from a cutoff
Global extrapolation from a local effect

sample_tasks.instruction: Specify and estimate a local economic regression with interpretable effects, robust uncertainty, and functional-form, heteroskedasticity, and influence checks; then add one density check for manipulation at the assignment cutoff.

Specify and diagnose local regressions around an eligibility cutoff, estimate the discontinuity with robust uncertainty, test manipulation and covariate continuity, assess bandwidth and functional-form sensitivity, use placebo cutoffs, and interpret the effect as local to the threshold.

sections.name: Time-Series Forecasting
sections.outcome: Diagnose temporal structure, construct probabilistic forecasts without leakage, and compare them with suitable baselines under realistic backtests.

sample_tasks.instruction: Identify the dominant seasonal pattern in a short series and produce one forecast from it.

For one demand series, diagnose trend, seasonality, lag dependence, gaps, and breaks; build forecasts and intervals from that structure; and compare them with baselines using rolling origins, calibration, subgroup errors, and operational loss.

sections.name: Temporal Structure Analysis
sections.outcome: Identify time indexing, trend, seasonality, autocorrelation, structural breaks, missing intervals, and external-event patterns that constrain valid forecasting.
excludes: Causal attribution of every temporal change

sample_tasks.instruction: Identify the dominant seasonal period in a regularly spaced series.

Analyze a multiyear operational series for indexing and spacing, trend, multiple seasonalities, autocorrelation, missing intervals, a structural break, and plausible external-event effects, and state the implications for forecasting.

sections.name: Forecast and Predictive-Uncertainty Construction
sections.outcome: Construct point and distributional forecasts from temporal features while preventing leakage and representing future-observation uncertainty.
excludes: Confidence intervals for fixed population parameters

sample_tasks.instruction: Using a supplied seasonal rule and past observations only, produce a one-step forecast and prediction interval.

Construct multi-horizon point and probabilistic forecasts for a seasonal series with exogenous inputs, defining leakage-free features and windows and explaining how parameter, innovation, and horizon uncertainty enter the prediction intervals.

sections.name: Forecast Backtesting and Selection
sections.outcome: Evaluate fully constructed probabilistic forecasts against suitable baselines using leakage-free rolling origins, calibration, subgroup errors, and decision-relevant loss.
excludes: Random train-test splits for ordered data

sample_tasks.instruction: Construct leakage-free point and distributional forecasts with prediction intervals for a short seasonal series, then add one rolling-origin comparison against a seasonal-naive baseline.

Construct multi-horizon point and probabilistic forecasts with leakage-free features and intervals, then compare them with suitable baselines over rolling origins, assess interval calibration and subgroup errors, and select a model using the stated operational loss.

sections.name: Visualization, Dashboards, and Reports
sections.outcome: Turn one analysis into faithful visual explanations, interactive monitoring views, and evidence-grounded reports tailored to a shared audience and decision.
excludes: Unrelated deliverables combined into a package

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose one faithful chart and write one evidence-supported sentence for a stated decision audience.

Using one completed retention analysis and one management decision, create a faithful annotated visual summary, an interactive monitoring dashboard, and a concise analytical report that use consistent metrics, uncertainty, limitations, and recommendations.

sections.name: Chart and Infographic Production
sections.outcome: Produce statistical charts and explanatory infographic compositions whose encodings, scales, annotations, hierarchy, and claims communicate quantitative evidence faithfully.

sample_tasks.instruction: Specify the marks, axes, scale, and labels for a chart comparing a numeric outcome across three groups.

Using one public-health dataset and explanatory message, construct a faithful chart showing the central comparison and uncertainty, then integrate that chart with concise annotations and supporting facts into an accessible infographic.

sections.name: Statistical Chart Design
sections.outcome: Select and construct chart encodings that faithfully reveal a stated distribution, comparison, relationship, uncertainty, or temporal pattern.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose and specify a chart for comparing one skewed outcome across categories.

Create a compact, accessible chart suite for one analysis that shows data coverage, distributions, subgroup comparisons, multivariable relationships, temporal change, and uncertainty without misleading scales or clutter.

sections.name: Infographic Composition
sections.outcome: Combine a faithful quantitative chart, calibrated claims, annotations, and visual hierarchy into a concise explanatory graphic for a defined audience.
excludes: Decorative illustration as the main product

sample_tasks.instruction: Construct a faithful, accessible chart with appropriate scales and uncertainty; state the supported finding, distinguish it from causal or mechanistic alternatives, and identify a limitation; then add a headline and reading order for a one-panel infographic.

For one multifactor trend, construct accessible charts with faithful scales and uncertainty, calibrate the descriptive, predictive, and causal wording against alternative explanations and design limitations, and compose the charts, headline, annotations, and notes into a clear infographic.

sections.name: Dashboard and Analytical Report Building
sections.outcome: Organize the same validated metrics and findings into an interactive monitoring dashboard and a decision-oriented analytical report.
excludes: Chart mechanics as the sole task
Dashboards and reports about unrelated questions

sample_tasks.instruction: Define one decision-relevant metric and express it as both a monitoring tile and a one-sentence analytical finding.
For one service-quality decision, build a dashboard for recurring monitoring and a report explaining the same metrics, trends, segments, uncertainty, limitations, exceptions, and recommended action.

sections.name: Dashboard Design
sections.outcome: Design dashboards whose faithful charts, validated metrics, hierarchy, filters, states, and drill-downs support recurring monitoring and diagnosis.

sample_tasks.instruction: Construct a faithful chart with appropriate marks, scales, labels, uncertainty, accessibility, and annotation for a monitoring question, then add one category filter with a clearly defined selected state.

Construct faithful charts for an operational monitoring question, then organize them with validated metric definitions, overview indicators, trend and segment views, useful filters and drill-downs, explicit freshness and missing-data states, and decision-linked alert thresholds.

sections.name: Analytical Report Writing
sections.outcome: Write a self-contained report connecting a question, data, methods, findings, uncertainty, limitations, and recommendations without exceeding the analysis.
excludes: Claims unsupported by the reported analysis

sample_tasks.instruction: From one raw dataset, diagnose quality, summarize distributions and groups, and investigate conditioned relationships; construct a faithful chart with uncertainty; distinguish the supported result from causal and mechanistic alternatives; then add one decision recommendation and its principal limitation.

Analyze one decision dataset through quality, distributional, grouped, and multivariable exploration; construct faithful tables and charts; calibrate descriptive, predictive, and causal claims against uncertainty and alternatives; and write a concise report covering the question, data, methods, findings, limitations, and proportionate recommendation.
